approvers: Nobody, I decide alone, but my site foreman and the glazing sub would have to agree to it
reason: I have never paid for this. We cover the glass with tape and film and cardboard, and when a pane gets damaged the glazier replaces it and we argue about whose fault it was. Paying around 19 euro a square metre on top of the job is margin I do not have, and I do not want another trade on site.
objection: In July and August half the facade is in full sun. When can you even apply it, and does it come off clean after months of heat and plaster? If it sticks to the frame or marks the glass, I pay twice. And 50% up front for a supplier I do not know does not work for me.
instead: Keep using cheap protection film and tape from the hardware store, keep the glazing sub responsible for damage, and keep fitting the windows as late as possible in the job.
would_change_my_mind: A contractor I know and trust, on a block like mine, telling me it came off clean after a summer and saved them real replacement claims. Then a trial on one block at much lower cost, with ACHV paying if the coating damages a frame.
